data.text/markdown:
Off-screen 3D rendering

MRPT describes 3D scenes with a scene graph (mrpt.viz): a Scene holds objects such as grids, boxes, point clouds, robot models or uncertainty ellipsoids. mrpt.opengl.CFBORender renders that scene into an image without any window or display, using EGL and an OpenGL framebuffer object (FBO). It returns the color image and the depth of every pixel, as NumPy arrays: useful to make figures, videos, or synthetic camera data on a headless server. The scene below shows a robot that has driven along a path, with the 95% confidence ellipsoids of its position growing as odometry errors accumulate. Move the sliders to orbit the camera: each frame is rendered on the server.

data.text/markdown:
The same scene can be shown in a desktop window with mrpt.gui.CDisplayWindowGUI, or saved to a file and opened later with MRPT's SceneViewer3D application.
Run it on your computer (Linux, Python 3.11 to 3.14, with the system OpenGL/EGL libraries): 
uvx marimo edit --sandbox https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MRPT/mrpt-notebooks/main/notebooks/offscreen_3d_rendering.py
More MRPT Python examples: mrpt_examples_py.
